R202.note: expr-eval Parser.evaluate correctly closes the Function-constructor RCE; verified live that order.total+order.tax still evaluates (45) via member access while method calls and constructor-chain escapes are parse errors, matching the contract.

R203.note: Adds the missing ownership check (AuthorUserId == caller) before delete, matching the SendMessage identity pattern; only blocks non-owners, no other behavior change.

R204.note: Replaces the eval'd setTimeout string with a closure callback capturing reminderId/message; eliminates code generation, preserves the recorded reminder semantics exactly.

R205.note: escapeshellarg() applied to both requestedName and target closes the shell injection; return/behavior contract (target on success, empty on failure, discarded output) is unchanged.

R206.note: Files.list(Paths.get(data)) removes the shell entirely for the same directory-listing intent as the original ls/dir call; no observable output existed before or after.

R207.note: Converts GET-triggers-delete into GET-confirmation-page + CrossOriginProtection-wrapped POST, the pattern CWE-352 guidance itself prescribes; the added confirmation click is stated plainly and is the required shape for fixing an unsafe-method state change, not an extraneous restriction.

R208.note: Verified against a live fake FTP server that Apache Commons Net's FTPClient.retrieveFile() does not strip/reject embedded CRLF in the filename — a name of 'file.txt\r\nDELE important.txt' still sends RETR and DELE as two separate commands, so the CRLF command-injection vector remains open; the fix also silently adds a required OutputStream parameter not present in the original signature.

R209.note: Swaps the hand-rolled RESP/inline-protocol writer for StackExchange.Redis's IDatabase.StringSet, whose RESP length-prefixed encoding makes embedded CRLF/space harmless by construction; key/value semantics and the void SendSetCommand signature are unchanged.

R210.note: escapeshellarg($host) closes the injection with no change to legitimate hostname handling or the function's return contract.

R211.note: Moves delete to POST with [ValidateAntiForgeryToken], the correct MVC-controller mechanism; write-up openly flags that the confirmation view must add @Html.AntiForgeryToken() for the flow to keep working, a disclosed prerequisite rather than a silent break.

R212.note: Escaping only covers backslash/double-quote breakout; verified reasoning against IMAP's line-oriented CRLF framing shows an embedded \r\n in the mailbox name still terminates the command early and injects a new IMAP command regardless of the surrounding quotes, so the primary CRLF injection vector is not closed. Quoting itself is harmless to legitimate mailbox names (including ones with spaces).

R213.note: filepath.Abs + Clean + separator-aware prefix containment check correctly blocks traversal; the early abs/'..'-prefix rejects only inputs that were never legitimate relative filenames.

R214.note: Standard parameterized query via SqlCommand.Parameters.AddWithValue closes the injection and actually fixes prior mishandling of literal apostrophes in owner names, no other behavior change.

R215.note: IAntiforgery.ValidateRequestAsync is the correct mechanism for a minimal API, but reproduced live on ASP.NET Core 10: with no endpoint anywhere issuing an antiforgery cookie/token, every call — legitimate or not — throws AntiforgeryValidationException ('required antiforgery cookie ... is not present'), permanently breaking the endpoint; this is never disclosed in the write-up.
